newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Jan 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Jan 9.

text.p: - Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- TAXPAYERS' WATCHDOG WILL INVESTIGATE HMSO SELL-OFF

The National Audit Office is to investigate the privatisation of Her Majesty's Safety Office, sold last October for 54 million stg. The final price was less than one-third of initial expectations, and the successful buyer was allowed extra time to negotiate after being named the preferred bidder.
-- GREEN LIGHT FOR SALE OF CCSB TO AMERICANS

The European Commission is expected to give formal clearance later this month to the proposed 1.85 billion dollar takeover of Coca-Cola & Schweppes Beverages by Coca-Cola Enterprises of the United States. The proposed deal would see the two brands promoted separately, but with Cadbury Schweppes ceasing downstream bottling and distribution. Competitors had complained to the Commission that the deal would give Coca-Cola an unfair dominance of the British market, but CCSB argued this only applied to the cola market, not the soft drink market generally.
THE TIMES -- LLOYDS FINED 325,000 STG FOR SELLING PENSIONS

Lloyds Bank has been fined 325,000 stg by a City watchdog, becoming the latest household name to be caught up in the four billion stg personal pension mis-selling scandal. Imro, the regulator for fund managers, said Lloyds Bank, the owners of TSB, had been found guilty of three serious rule breaches on pension transfer business, the infringements relating to investors being wrongly advised to transfer money held on their behalf in occupational schemes into a personal pension between April 1988 and June 1993.
-- DIXONS FEARS TAX WILL HIT PROFITS

Electrical retailer Dixons warned that a change in taxation rules on extended warranties could hit profits next year, with customers picking up some of the costs in higher prices. The group said an increase in insurance premium tax to 17.5 percent from 2.5 percent from April is meant to apply to extended warranties, which account for around 8.5 percent of group sales, as well as 10 percent of pre-tax profits.
-- NU WITH-PROFITS PAYOUT FIXED AT RECORD 870 MILLION STG

Norwich Union, the mutual insurer planning to float on the Stock Exchange this year, is to pay out more than 870 million stg to around 53,000 members with mature with-profits policies, its largest payout on such policies. However, although the insurer has maintained bonus rates, these have dropped below those of its rival insurers, Friends Provident and General Accident.
THE GUARDIAN
-- SEARS TO ISSUE NEW PROFITS WARNING

Despite recent good times in the high street market, retailing group Sears is about to publish a fresh profits warning. The company is understood to be about to tell investors that profits for the current financial year are 20 percent below City expectations of about 100 million stg. Some institutional investors were planning a campaign to remove chief executive Liam Strong.
-- HULL'S MUNICIPAL PHONE COMPANY TO CUT JOBS

About 800 jobs are expected to be cut at Hull's municipally- owned telephone company, Kingston Communications. The company is the last council-owned telephone business in Britain. The company is seeking a first wave of 300 redundancies as part of a restructuring as a result of new technologies being introduced.
-- PHILIPS GIVES UP GRUNDIG BATTLE AFTER 570 MILLION STG LOSSES

Philips yesterday gave up management control of German television and video recorder maker Grundig after losses of 570 million stg since 1984. The company said it wanted to concentrate on a single brand name. It is also attempting to withdraw from an agreement which means it pays majority shareholder the Max Grundig Foundation an annual dividend of 19 million stg and has to buy the foundation's stake for 200 million stg in 2004.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- WATER PLEDGES DRAW FIRE ALL ROUND

The privatised water industry came under attack despite making pledges to end hosepipe bans and share gains, made from future efficiency, with customers. An end to the discharge of untreated sewage into rivers and the sea was also promised. But the campaign by nine of the 10 privatised water companies backfired after they were unable to give a firm date for when hosepipe bans would stop or give firm details on how future gains would be divided between customers and shareholders.
-- WARNING OF LOWER PROFITS HITS TC SHARES

Britain's largest nursing home operator, TC Group, saw its shares sink to their lowest level for eight years yesterday, following the group's warning that continuing difficulties in filling new homes would hit profits. The warning comes just four months after the creation of TC from the merger of Takare and Court Cavendish in September, and a statement in November claiming that trading and occupancy for the enlarged group had been maintained at levels set out at the time of the merger. Shares fell 25p to 114.5p.
-- BRITISH CAR MAKERS ACCELERATE WORLD SALES DESPITE STRONG STG

Britain's car makers recorded a big increase in worldwide sales last year despite the effects of the strong pound. Rover had total sales of over half a million for the first time in eight years and Rolls Royce reported a 12 percent jump in sales, due largely to the success of the Bentley range. Jaguar reported a slight fall in sales but this was due to a six-month wait between the end of XJS production in April and the launch of the new sports model XK8 in October.
